recommendedTextbook.title: A Guide to WASSCE/SSCE Literature-in-English
recommendedTextbook.author: Kola Eke
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: Introduction to Literature and the Three Genres
subtopics: Definition and societal functions of literature (didactic, aesthetic, social mirror, historical chronicle)
The three genres: Prose (fiction, non-fiction), Drama (tragedy, comedy, tragicomedy), Poetry (lyric, epic, ballad, elegy)
Distinction between prose narrative, dramatic dialogue, and poetic verse
objectives: Define literature in relation to human culture and oral folklore
Differentiate the characteristics and structural layouts of prose, drama, and poetry
Identify 4 ways in which literature fosters moral discipline and empathy in secondary school learners

topics.topic: Literary Devices: Figures of Speech and Sound Devices
subtopics: Figures of comparison: Simile, metaphor, personification, apostrophe
Figures of contrast and association: Antithesis, oxymoron, irony, metonymy, synecdoche, hyperbole, litotes
Sound devices in verse: Alliteration, assonance, consonance, onomatopoeia, rhyme, rhythm
objectives: Identify 10 distinct literary devices in given poetic stanzas
Explain the difference between verbal irony, situational irony, and dramatic irony
Construct original sentences illustrating synecdoche and metonymy

topics.topic: Elements of Prose Fiction: Plot, Setting and Point of View
subtopics: Elements of prose: Plot structure (exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, denouement)
Setting: Spatial (geographical), temporal (historical era), and socio-cultural milieu
Narrative points of view: First-person, third-person limited, third-person omniscient, stream of consciousness
objectives: Chart the narrative plot arc of a prescribed introductory African novella
Analyze the influence of physical and cultural setting on character behavior
Contrast an omniscient narrator with an unreliable first-person protagonist

topics.topic: Elements of Drama: Conflict, Characterization and Stage Conventions
subtopics: Dramatic elements: Dialogue, soliloquy, aside, dramatic irony, chorus
Characterization: Protagonist, antagonist, foil, round vs flat characters, tragic flaw (hamartia)
Stage conventions: Stage directions, props, costume, lighting, and theatrical staging
objectives: Explain the dramatic purpose of a soliloquy in revealing interior psychology
Identify the central dramatic conflict (interpersonal, internal, environmental) in an African play extract
Analyze how a foil character highlights the tragic protagonist's fatal flaw
